correctness.rationale: For omega>0 and real |epsilon|<1, the half-line row-weighted Hilbert matrix differs by a Hilbert-Schmidt cell-discretization and compact averaging/multiplier terms from the Carleman compression. The logarithmic change of variable gives convolution with K(t)=1/[2cosh(t/2)]; translations by a full modulation period furnish weak-null norm witnesses proving half-line essential norm equals the full-line norm. Positive periodic multiplier bounds all Floquet fibers by the zero-phase fiber, whose Fourier matrix is B=(I+epsilon(S+S*)/2)diag(pi sech(pi omega j)). Norm-perturbation and the finite-section tail yield the certified bound. The simple top eigenvalue of B*B at epsilon=0 and two ±1 couplings give quadratic coefficient (1+3r²)/(4(1-r²)); sign-conjugation eliminates odd orders. Independent finite sections tested several omega and amplitudes; infinite assertions rest on functional analysis, not numerical SVD.
residual_risks: Fixed omega>0 asymptotics not uniform as omega tends to 0; neither essential spectrum nor other sequence spaces classified.
